50.s: Under which Article of the Constitution of India are taxes levied and collected by the centre and assigned to the states?
50.x: Under Article 269 taxes on inter-State sale and consignment of goods are levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States. Art. 268A (service tax) was omitted, 270 is the shared pool and 271 surcharges.

50.s:
Consider the following statements in connection with the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and the States:

I. The proceeds of the surcharges levied on taxes and duties referred to in Article 269 and Article 270 of the Constitution of India, would be shared between the Centre and the States.

II. Article 268A and Article 272 of the Constitution of India were both repealed by same Constitutional Amendment Act.

III. Tax on the sale of petroleum crude is levied by the Centre but collected by the States.

IV. The net proceeds of tax categories that are falling under Article 269 of the Constitution of India, do not form a part of the Consolidated Fund of India.
Which of the above statement/statements is/are valid?
50.x: Only IV is valid: Art. 269 proceeds do not form part of the CFI. I is wrong because Art. 271 surcharges go wholly to the Union; II is wrong because Art. 272 was omitted by the 80th Amendment (2000) and 268A by the 101st (2016); III is wrong because tax on the sale of petroleum crude is levied by the States (State List).

50.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the levying, collecting and distribution of Income Tax is correct?
o: The Union levies, collects and distributes the proceeds of income tax between itself and the States
The Union levies, collects and keeps all the proceeds of income tax to itself
The Union levies and collects the tax but all the proceeds are distributed among the States
Only the surcharge levied on income tax is shared between the Union and the States
50.x: Income tax (other than on agricultural income) is levied and collected by the Union and its net proceeds are distributed between the Union and the States under Art. 270 on the Finance Commission's advice; only the surcharge stays with the Union.

50.s: Under which Article of the Constitution of India, Taxes are levied and collected by the centre but distributed between the centre and the States?
50.x: Article 270 covers taxes levied and collected by the Union and distributed between the Union and the States. Art. 268 taxes are collected by the States, 269 taxes are assigned to the States and 271 surcharges are kept by the Union.

50.s: In India non-agricultural income tax is
o: levied by the Centre and fully distributed among the States.
levied and appropriated by the Centre.
levied by the Centre and shared with the States.
50.x: Non-agricultural income tax is levied by the Centre and shared with the States (Art. 270 divisible pool). It is not kept wholly by the Centre, nor given wholly to the States; only agricultural income tax is a State tax.

50.s: Excise tax on liquor is levied by
50.x: Excise duty on alcoholic liquor for human consumption is a State List subject (Entry 51), levied and retained by the State Government.

50.s: Which of the following tax is levied by Union and collected and appropriated by States?
50.x: Under Art. 268 stamp duties on bills of exchange, cheques, insurance policies etc. are levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States. Estate duty and taxes on newspapers were old Art. 269 items (now Art. 270 / GST).

50.s:
Consider the following statements- In India taxes on transactions in Stock-Exchanges and Futures Markets are –
1. Levied by Union.
2. Collected by the State Government.
50.x: Taxes (other than stamp duty) on stock-exchange and futures-market transactions are Union List Entry 90 – levied and collected by the Union (old Art. 269, now the Art. 270 pool). They are not collected by the States, so only statement 1 is correct.

50.s: Under constitutional provision of tax assignment in India, which of the following is a tax exclusively imposed and collected by the states?
50.x: Land revenue (State List Entry 45) is imposed and collected exclusively by the States. Income tax and corporation tax are Union taxes and GST is shared.

50.s: Which of the following is levied and collected by the Centre, but assigned to the States?
50.x:
Most books and keys: taxes on railway fares (original Art. 269). Strictly, since the 80th Amendment (2000) railway-fare taxes are in the Art. 270 pool; today Art. 269 covers only taxes on inter-State sale and consignment of goods.
the 80th Amendment (2000) moved railway-fare taxes from Art. 269 into the Art. 270 divisible pool — now Art. 269 assigns to the States only taxes on inter-State sale/purchase and consignment of goods (Laxmikanth Ch15).
Taxes on railway fares and freights were levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States under the original Art. 269 – the textbook answer. Customs and income tax are shared Union taxes and stamp duty is collected by the States.

50.s: Agriculture Income Tax is assigned to the State Government by-
50.x: Tax on agricultural income is assigned to the States by the Constitution itself (State List Entry 46). The Finance Commission, NDC and Inter-State Council cannot assign taxes.

50.s: Excise duty obtained on alcoholic medicines used by people is a source of revenue for whom?
o: Source of revenue of the Centre
Source of revenue of the States
Source of revenue of the Union Territories
Source of revenue of both the Central and State governments
50.x:
the 101st Amendment (2016) removed excise on medicinal and toilet preparations from Art. 268 — now such preparations are taxed under GST (CGST + SGST) (Laxmikanth Ch15 p.231).
Before GST, excise on medicinal and toilet preparations containing alcohol was levied by the Union but collected and kept by the States (Art. 268), so it was State revenue (now, under GST, not an Art. 268 duty).

50.s: Under which of the following taxes the total amount payable by an individual is limited by the Constitution?
o: Tax on profession, trade, and callings
50.x: Art. 276(2) caps the total tax on professions, trades, callings and employments payable by any person at ₹2,500 a year – the only such ceiling in the Constitution.

50.s: Which one of the following taxes is imposed and charged by the Union, but is divided into Union and the States?
o: Taxes on items except for agriculture income
Taxes on railway fares and freights
50.x:
Printed key: Customs. Strictly, since the 80th Amendment (2000, from 1996) corporation tax and customs are also in the Art. 270 pool; income tax is the classic answer and the only one that fits under the Constitution before 1996.
'Taxes on income other than agricultural income' is the tax the Union levies and collects but shares with the States (Art. 270) – the only one shared under the original Constitution. Railway-fare taxes were assigned wholly to the States, and corporation tax and customs became shareable only with the 80th Amendment.

50.s: Which Article of the Constitution empowers the States to levy tax on professions, trades, callings and employments?
50.x: Article 276 deals with profession tax; the ceiling is Rs 2,500 per person per year.

50.s: Which of the following sets contains only taxes or levies associated with the State domain?
o: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles
Customs duty, corporation tax, Union excise duty and income tax
Goods and Services Tax, customs duty, wealth tax and corporation tax
Surcharge on Union taxes, customs duty, export duty and corporation tax
50.x: Land revenue, agricultural income tax, State excise on alcohol and taxes on vehicles are included among taxes associated with the State domain. The other sets consist predominantly of Union taxes.
50.tq: Separate the State tax field from familiar Union taxes by checking every item in the set.
xs: **Land revenue, agricultural income tax, state excise on alcohol, vehicle taxes** are all **state-only** taxes — option **(1)**.
**Customs**, **corporation tax**, **income tax** and **surcharges** are **Union** taxes.
xa: Other state-only taxes: **stamp duties and registration**, taxes on **land and buildings**, **mineral rights**, **electricity** consumption, **professions**.
**Agricultural income tax**: **States** only (UPPSC 2009).
**Excise on liquor**: **States** (UPPSC 2014).

50.s: Under Article 268 (e.g. stamp duties on specified instruments), how are duties levied, collected and appropriated?
o: Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
Levied and collected by the States but appropriated by the Union
Levied by the States and collected jointly by the Union and the States
Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
50.x: Article 268 covers duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States.
xa: ⚠ **269** = Union collects, **assigned to states**; **271** surcharges = **Centre only**.
Excise on **medicinal/toilet preparations** under 268 ended with GST.
**268A** (service tax, **88th Amendment, 2003**) was **omitted by the 101st Amendment, 2016**.

50.s: Under Article 269, how are taxes on the inter-State sale or purchase of goods (other than newspapers) levied and shared?
o: Levied and collected by the States and appropriated by them
Levied and collected by the Union but assigned to the States
Levied, collected and appropriated exclusively by the Union
Levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
50.x: Under Article 269 the Union levies and collects these taxes (including taxes on consignment of goods) and assigns them to the States.
xa: ⚠ Collected and appropriated by states = **Art. 268** (stamp duties).
**Art. 269A**: **IGST** on inter-state supplies.
**Art. 271** surcharges: **exclusively for the Union**.

50.s: What happens to the proceeds of a surcharge levied on a tax covered by Article 270?
o: automatically divided between the Union and States
collected and kept by the State concerned
distributed on the GST Council's recommendation
50.x: Under Article 271, surcharges on Article 269 and 270 taxes are for Union purposes and are not shared with the States.
xa: Art. 271 surcharges are on **Art. 269/270** taxes.
Non-shareable **cesses and surcharges** cut effective devolution to near **31-32%** vs the **41%** award.
Art. 270 pool is shared on **FC** recommendation.

50.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Article 269 — Surcharge exclusively for the Union
Article 270 — Stamp duties collected and appropriated by States
50.x: Article 269A concerns IGST on inter-State supplies. Article 268 covers specified stamp duties, Article 269 covers assigned taxes, and Article 271 covers surcharges.
50.tq: Discriminate among closely placed Articles by matching each Article with its distinctive tax arrangement.
xs: **Art. 269A** — **IGST**, i.e. **GST on inter-state supplies** — option **(3)**.
**268** = **stamp duties** collected by states; **269** = taxes **assigned** to states; surcharges for the Union = **271**.
xa: 269A revenue goes to the **destination state**.
269A was inserted by the **101st Amendment, 2016**.
IGST is shared as Parliament provides on **GST Council** advice.

50.s: Since which Constitutional Amendment has corporation tax, levied and collected by the Union, been shared with the States?
50.x: Since the 80th Constitutional Amendment, corporation tax is part of the shareable pool of Union taxes.
xa: 80th CAA effective **1 April 1996**; enacted the **10th FC's** scheme.
**Customs duty** too is now in the divisible pool (**Art. 270**).
Net proceeds certified by the **CAG**.

50.s: Which taxes does Article 270 cover?
o: all Union List taxes without exception
only customs duties and Union excise duties
all State List taxes collected by the Union
Union taxes shared via the Finance Commission, excluding specified taxes, surcharges and cesses
50.x: Article 270 covers Union List taxes shared as recommended by the Finance Commission, excluding Article 268, 269 and 269A taxes, Article 271 surcharges and cesses.
xa: States' share: **41%** of the divisible pool (**15th FC**; retained by **16th FC**).
**Customs duty** is now in the divisible pool.
Net proceeds certified by the **CAG**.

50.s: Service tax was associated with Article 268A before that Article was omitted by which Constitutional Amendment?
50.x: Article 268A was introduced for service tax by the 88th Amendment in 2003 and was omitted by the 101st Amendment in 2016 with the introduction of GST.
50.tq: Pair the provision with the amendment that removed it, not the amendment that introduced it.
xs: **Art. 268A** (service tax) was **omitted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016** — option **(3)**.
It had been added by the **88th Amendment, 2003**; service tax was replaced by **GST**.
xa: 101st Amendment inserted **246A, 269A, 279A**.
**80th CAA, 2000** omitted **Art. 272**.
GST from **1 July 2017**.

50.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the authority that levies it?
50.x: Excise on liquor is a State tax. Customs duty is levied by the Union, agricultural income tax by the States, and entertainment tax is largely subsumed in GST except for local bodies.
50.tq: Use the “who levies the tax?” test to distinguish Union and State revenue sources.
xs: **Excise on liquor** is levied by the **states** — option **(3)**.
**Customs** is a **Union** tax; **agricultural income tax** is **states** only; **entertainment tax** is a state tax largely subsumed in GST.
xa: Excise on liquor = UPPSC 2014; agricultural income tax = **UPPSC 2009**.
**Customs** is not a state tax revenue (**JPSC 2013**).
**Land revenue** is a **state** tax.

50.s: What is true of the proceeds of taxes under Article 269 that are assigned to the States?
o: Do not form part of the Consolidated Fund of India
Are shared on the GST Council's advice
Are kept by the Union as surcharges
Form part of the divisible pool under Article 270
50.x: Article 269 taxes are collected by the Union and assigned to the States, and their proceeds do not form part of the CFI.
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: Which of the following is NOT a tax levied only by the States?
50.x: Corporation tax is levied by the Union, never by the States; land revenue, agricultural income tax and liquor excise are State taxes.
50.tq: NOT

50.s: Which one of the following was NOT folded into the Article 270 pool by the 80th Constitutional Amendment?
o: Taxes on stock-exchange transactions other than stamp duty
50.x: Pre-2000 taxes on stock-exchange transactions, estate duty, railway fares and newspapers were folded into the Article 270 pool. Surcharges remain exclusively for the Union under Article 271.
50.tq: Identify the item expressly excluded from the divisible pool.
xs: **Surcharges** were not folded in — they stay **exclusively for the Union** under **Art. 271** — option **(1)**.
The **80th CAA** folded pre-2000 Art. 269 taxes — **stock-exchange transactions**, **estate duty**, **railway fares**, newspapers — into the **Art. 270** pool.
xa: PYQ trap: surcharges under Art. 271 are **not shared** with states (APPSC-G1 2024).
Art. 270 excludes **268, 269, 269A** taxes, **surcharges** and **cesses**.
Non-shareable cesses ~**18%** of Centre's gross tax revenue.

50.s: On whose advice are the proceeds of IGST on inter-State supply apportioned between the Centre and the States?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
50.x: Article 269A provides for apportionment of IGST on inter-State supply between the Centre and the States on the advice of the GST Council.
50.tq: Identify the constitutional body associated with the specific tax-distribution mechanism.
xs: **IGST** proceeds are shared as Parliament provides on **GST Council** advice (**Art. 269A**) — option **(1)**.
Revenue goes to the **destination state**.
xa: **GST Council** = **Art. 279A**; chaired by the **Union Finance Minister**.
Art. 270 pool includes the **Centre's share of IGST**.
GST components: **CGST, SGST, IGST, UTGST**.

50.s: Which Article of the Constitution concerns the Integrated GST (IGST)?
50.x: Article 269A, added by the 101st Amendment, deals with IGST; Article 270 covers taxes shared between the Centre and the States.
n: Article 269A concerns IGST. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
IGST is associated with the 101st Constitutional Amendment. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 270 concerns taxes shared between the Centre and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]

50.s: Which authority has the power to recommend the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
50.src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
50.x: The Finance Commission (Art. 280) recommends how the net proceeds of shareable taxes are divided between the Union and the States. The CAG only certifies the net proceeds; the GST Council advises on GST, not on the divisible pool.

50.s: Which one of the following authorities recommends the principles governing the grants‑in‑aid of the revenues to the states out of the Consolidated Fund of India?
50.x: Under Art. 280(3)(b) the Finance Commission recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid to States out of the CFI. The Inter-State Council, Finance Ministry and PAC have no such constitutional role.

50.s: The financial resource between Centre and State is distributed on
50.x: The sharing of tax revenue between the Centre and States (Arts 270, 275) follows the Finance Commission's recommendations under Art. 280, not those of the Finance Ministry, RBI or NABARD.

50.s: Inter se distribution of tax shares, by the Finance Commission, amongst the states is known as:
50.src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
50.x: The Finance Commission's division of the divisible pool between the Centre and the States is vertical devolution; the inter se distribution among the States is horizontal distribution (Art. 280(3)(a)).

50.s: Compositional shift from grants to tax devolution from Centre to State causes
o: additional fiscal burden on the Centre
increase in share of unconditional transfers to States
demand from States to increase tax rates
lack of fiscal space to carry out specific purpose transfer to States
50.x: Tax devolution is untied money the States may spend as they choose, while grants are often conditional, so a shift from grants to devolution (14th FC) raises the share of unconditional transfers.

50.s: The percentage of distribution of revenue from taxes between the Centre and the States is recommended by the
50.x: The Finance Commission (Art. 280) recommends the sharing of tax revenue between the Centre and the States; NITI Aayog, the Inter-State Council and the NDC have no such role.

50.s: With reference to the Finance Commission of India, which of the following statements is correct?
o: It encourages the inflow of foreign capital for
It facilitates the proper distribution of finances among
It ensures transparency in financial administration
50.x: Under Art. 280(3) the Finance Commission recommends tax devolution, grants-in-aid principles and local-body resources; it does not attract foreign capital, distribute funds among PSUs or ensure transparency in administration, so none of the statements is correct.

50.s: The principles concerning the provisions of the grants-in-aid to the states out of the Consolidated Fund of India are recommended by the
50.x: The principles governing grants-in-aid to States out of the CFI are recommended by the Finance Commission (Art. 280(3)(b)), not the Planning Commission, NDC or ARC.

50.s: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body established under which Article of the Constitution?
50.x: The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial constitutional body under Article 280, in Part XII. Article 275 deals with grants and 282 with discretionary grants.
50.tq: Recall Article 280.
n: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission is a quasi-judicial body. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 concerns the Finance Commission. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 is located in Part XII of the Constitution. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Finance Commission has a quasi-judicial character. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
The Union Finance Commission is governed by Article 280. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 280 belongs to Part XII. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xs: The **Finance Commission** is set up under **Article 280** — option **(4)** is correct.
**Article 281** deals with its **report / recommendations**; **Article 275** = **grants-in-aid**; **Article 282** = **discretionary grants**.
xa: **Article 275** grants: **principles** recommended by the Finance Commission.
⚠ Statutory grants are **not** on **NITI Aayog's** advice (APPSC-GS 2019).

50.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: It retained the vertical share of States in the divisible pool at 41%
The Union Government accepted this recommendation in Budget 2026–27
Vertical share refers to distribution of the divisible pool among individual States
Distribution of the divisible pool among individual States is inter se devolution
50.x: Vertical devolution concerns the Centre–State share; distribution among individual States is inter se (horizontal) devolution.
xa: Non-shareable cesses (~**18%** of gross tax revenue) cut effective devolution to about **31-32%**.
The **16th FC** caps state fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP**.

50.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended what share of the divisible pool for the States?
50.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended 41 percent; 42 percent was the Fourteenth Finance Commission's figure.
xa: Non-shareable cesses are about **18%** of the Centre's gross tax revenue.
The **10th FC** gave the "**Alternative Scheme of Devolution**", enacted by the **80th CAA, 2000**.
Under that scheme the states' share was **29%** = **26%** + **3%** in lieu of additional excise duties.
**Art. 280** creates the Finance Commission; **Art. 281** deals with its recommendations.

50.s: What did the 2024 'Chalo Delhi' protest by southern States mainly oppose?
o: the replacement of grants by cesses
the abolition of State Development Loans
conditionality attached to Centrally Sponsored Schemes only
50.x: The protest concerned the perceived adverse effect of population-heavy or population-based criteria on the devolution share of southern States.
50.tq: Identify the policy issue represented by the protest instead of confusing it with other fiscal criticisms.
xs: The **2024 "Chalo Delhi"** protest by southern states was against **population-based criteria in devolution** — option **(3)** is correct.
Southern states objected to **population-heavy** devolution criteria.
xa: Gadgil-type formulas weighted **population** at **60%**.
Other debates: **vertical fiscal imbalance**, **CSS conditionality**, and **non-shareable cesses**.
AP's memorandum to the **16th FC** sought extra weight for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** (**Feb 2026**).

50.s: What does horizontal devolution of the divisible pool refer to?
o: Between the Centre and the States
Between the States and local bodies
50.x: Vertical devolution is the Centre-State share; horizontal devolution is distribution among the States, both recommended by the Finance Commission.
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: Under which Article does the Finance Commission recommend both vertical and horizontal devolution?
50.x: Article 280(3) tasks the Finance Commission with both the Centre-State share and its distribution among States.
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: Because cesses and surcharges stay outside the divisible pool, what is the effective devolution to States?
50.x: Cesses and surcharges, about 18% of gross tax revenue, stay outside the pool, so effective devolution is near 31-32% against the 41% award.
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: Which one of the following is associated with the recommendations of the Sixteenth Finance Commission regarding State finances?
o: A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GDP for the Union alone
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 5% of GSDP and expansion of off-budget borrowing
A fiscal deficit ceiling of 3% of GSDP and ending off-budget borrowing
A prohibition on all State borrowing from domestic sources
50.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission caps the State fiscal deficit at 3% of GSDP and calls for ending off-budget borrowing.
50.tq: Match the numerical ceiling with the correct level of government and fiscal practice.
xs: The **16th FC** caps the state fiscal deficit at **3% of GSDP** and calls for **ending off-budget borrowing** — option **(3)** is correct.
It concerns **State** finances, not the Union alone; it seeks to end, not expand, off-budget borrowing.
xa: The **16th FC** (**2026-31**) retained the states' share at **41%**; the Centre **accepted** its devolution recommendations.
The **Net Borrowing Ceiling** already **counts off-budget borrowings**.
AP's memorandum to the 16th FC sought extra weight for **capital-city and infrastructure costs** after bifurcation (**Feb 2026**).

50.s: Which Finance Commission raised the States' share to 42% with a compositional shift towards unconditional transfers?
50.x: The Fourteenth FC gave 42% with more devolution and fewer grants, making transfers more unconditional (APPSC-G1 2017).
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: What was the tax devolution to the States in 2024-25?
50.x: Tax devolution in 2024-25 was Rs 12.87 lakh crore against a Budget Estimate of Rs 12.47 lakh crore.

50.s: What is the main effect on the States of a shift from grants to tax devolution?
o: More untied funds and greater fiscal autonomy for the States
More conditional transfers tied to central schemes
A fall in the States' share of central taxes
Higher matching shares for Centrally Sponsored Schemes
50.x: Devolution is formula-based and untied, so a shift from grants to devolution gives States more unconditional money and autonomy.

50.s: Provisions for grants from Union to States is specified under:
50.src: General Overview of the Indian Constitution & Welfare Paper-
50.x: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid from the Union to States in need, charged on the CFI and given on the Finance Commission's advice. Art. 205 is supplementary State grants, 224 additional HC judges and 344 the Official Language Commission.

50.s: Which article of the Constitution states that "No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law"?
50.src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
50.x: Article 265 says no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law. Art. 266 is the Consolidated Fund and Public Accounts, 267 the Contingency Fund and 264 the interpretation clause of Part XII.

50.s: The Article of the Constitution that provides for the establishment of Union Finance Commission:
50.x: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President under Article 280. Art. 360 is Financial Emergency; 287 and 289 deal with electricity taxes and exemption of State property.

50.s: The financial relations between the Union Government and States have been discussed under –
50.x: Chapter I of Part XII, 'Distribution of Revenues between the Union and the States', runs from Article 268 to Article 281; financial relations as a whole are Arts 268-293.

50.s: Provision for Descretionary Grant which may be given by Central government to States is given under which Article of the Constitution?
50.x: Article 282 lets the Union (or a State) make grants for any public purpose, even outside its legislative field – the discretionary grants. Art. 275 is statutory grants and 281 the laying of the FC report.

50.s: Which of the Constitutional Provision lays down that taxes can neither be levied nor collected without the authority of law?
50.x: Article 265: no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law. Art. 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds, 300 with suits, and 368 with amendment.

50.s: Which Article of Indian Constitution provides the scheme of the distribution of revenue between the Union and the States?
50.src: APPSC Extension Officer in Women & CW 2012
50.x: Part XII Chapter I, 'Distribution of Revenues between the Union and the States', begins at Article 268 (Arts 268-281). Arts 265-267 deal with taxation by law, the Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund.

50.s: Who certifies the net proceeds relevant to the divisible pool?
o: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
50.x: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India certifies the net proceeds used in determining the divisible pool.
50.tq: Use the institutional-responsibility approach: identify who certifies rather than who recommends devolution.
xs: **Net proceeds** are certified by the **Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG)** — option **(4)**.
The FC recommends the sharing; the CAG certifies the proceeds.
xa: Divisible pool = **Art. 270** taxes.
**CAG's State Finances 2023-24** report is in current relevance.

50.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Article 265 – No tax except by authority of law
Article 266 – Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts
Article 268 – Contingency Fund of a State
50.x: Article 268 deals with duties levied by the Union but collected by the States; Contingency Funds are under Article 267.
n: Part XII covers Articles 265 to 267. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 161-164]
Article 265 provides that no tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 161-164]
Article 266 deals with the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 161-164]
Article 267 deals with the Contingency Funds of the Union and the States. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #61 · pp 161-164]
xa: **Art. 270** = taxes **shared** between Centre and States.
**Art. 275** = **grants-in-aid**; **Art. 280** = **Finance Commission**.

50.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
50.x: Article 267 covers the Contingency Fund. Article 148 is the CAG, Article 266 the Consolidated Fund and Article 269A IGST.
n: Article 148 concerns the Comptroller and Auditor General. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 266 concerns the Consolidated Fund. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 267 concerns the Contingency Fund. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
Article 269A concerns IGST. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #26 · pp 65-68]
xa: **Art. 269A** came from the **101st Constitutional Amendment**.
**Art. 265:** no tax except by **authority of law**.
**Art. 279A** = **GST Council**.

50.s: Which Article exempts the property of the Union from taxation by the States?
50.x: Article 285 exempts Union property from State taxes; Article 289 exempts State property from Union taxes.

50.s: Which Article provides for the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts of India and of the States?
50.x: Article 266 provides for the Consolidated Funds and Public Accounts; Article 267 is about Contingency Funds.
50.tq: one-liner

50.s: Why can neither the Union nor the States alone carry a decision in the GST Council?
o: Because the Union Finance Minister does not vote in the Council
Because the States have a veto over all GST matters
Because the Council requires unanimous approval in every matter
Because the Centre has one-third and the States together have two-thirds of the weighted votes, while three-fourths is required
50.x: A GST Council decision needs three-fourths of the weighted votes. The Centre holds only one-third and all States together only two-thirds, so neither side can reach three-fourths alone; options A-C misstate the voting rules.
50.tq: Apply the voting weights and threshold instead of recalling either figure in isolation.
xs: **Centre one-third**, **states together two-thirds**; decisions need **three-fourths** of weighted votes — option **(4)**.
So **neither side** can carry a decision alone.
xa: ⚠ **1/3 – 2/3 – 3/4** = **Centre – states – majority needed**.

Members: Union **MoS (Finance)** + **State Finance Ministers**.

51.s: Which one of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides that "It shall be the duty of the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance"?
51.x: Article 355 imposes on the Union the duty to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance and to ensure governance per the Constitution. Art. 215 makes HCs courts of record, 275 is grants and 325 the electoral roll.

51.s:

51.x: Two are correct: Art. 355 makes the Union duty-bound to protect States against internal disturbance, and Art. 22(3) denies persons under preventive detention the right to counsel. Statement 3 is wrong – POTA s.32 made a confession to a police officer of SP rank or above admissible.

51.s: What would be the consequence if the State Governments fail to comply with the directions of the Central Government with regard to the exercise of their Administrative Power?

Consider the following:

60.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes vertical and horizontal devolution?
o: Vertical devolution is between Union and States; horizontal devolution is among the States
Vertical devolution concerns taxes; horizontal devolution concerns borrowing alone
Vertical devolution is among States; horizontal devolution is between Union and States
Both terms refer only to grants to local bodies
60.x: Vertical devolution divides the divisible pool between the Union and States, while horizontal devolution distributes the States' share among the States.
60.tq: Discriminate between two closely related fiscal terms by their direction of distribution.
xs: **Vertical devolution** = share of the **divisible pool** going from the **Union to States**; **horizontal devolution** = allocation of that share **among States** by a formula — option **(1)**.
Option (3) reverses the two terms.
xa: ⚠ The divisible pool (**Art. 270** taxes) **excludes cesses and surcharges**.
Vertical shares: **13th FC 32%**, **14th FC 42%**, **15th FC 41%**.
Highest horizontal weight in every FC: **income distance**.

60.s: Why does vertical fiscal imbalance arise in India?
o: Some States have higher per capita income than others
The States have the more buoyant taxes while the Union carries heavier spending duties
The Union has the more buoyant taxes while States carry heavier spending duties
The Union and the States have identical tax bases
60.x: The Centre controls the more buoyant taxes, while States bear major spending duties such as health, education, agriculture and police.
xa: Vertical devolution of the **divisible pool** corrects this imbalance.
⚠ Divisible pool **excludes cesses and surcharges** — a "shrinking divisible pool" is a criticism.
**18 states** had sought **50%** (Aug **2026**).

60.s: Which one of the following is excluded from the divisible pool of Central taxes?

xs: **Cesses and surcharges** are **excluded** from the divisible pool — option **(1)**.
The divisible pool is made up of **Art. 270** taxes, excluding cesses and surcharges.
xa: Vertical devolution = States' share of this pool; horizontal = its allocation **among States**.
Criticism: a **shrinking divisible pool**.
16th FC kept the States' share at **41%**.

xs: The **16th FC** was chaired by **Dr Arvind Panagariya** — option **(2)**.
**Y.V. Reddy** chaired the **14th FC** and **N.K. Singh** the **15th FC**.
xa: 16th FC constituted **31 Dec 2023**; report tabled **1 Feb 2026**; award **1 Apr 2026 – 31 Mar 2031**.
The 14th FC was constituted on **2 Jan 2013**.
16th FC added **contribution to GDP** (**10**) and dropped **revenue deficit grants**.

60.s: What weight did the Fourteenth Finance Commission give to income distance?

14th FC chair: **Y.V. Reddy**; vertical share **42%**.

60.x: The Fifteenth Finance Commission gave population (2011) a weight of 15 per cent; demographic performance carried 12.5 per cent.

xs: The **13th FC** gave **income distance** (which it called **fiscal capacity distance**) **47.5** — option **(1)**.
Its **population 1971** weight was **25**, not 17.5; **17.5** was the 14th FC's population 1971 weight.
xa: Area **15** was the weight in the **14th** and **15th** FCs.
Income distance was the **highest weight in every FC**: 47.5 → **50** → **45** → **42.5**.
13th FC vertical share: **32%**.

60.s: Which one of the following correctly describes a change introduced by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
o: Demographic performance was measured by total fertility rate alone.
Income distance was calculated from the average of the three largest States.
Forest cover excluded open forests from consideration.

60.x: The Sixteenth Finance Commission calculated income distance from the average of the top three large States. Its demographic-performance measure was population growth from 1971 to 2011; forest included open forests; and contribution to GDP replaced tax effort.

xs: The **16th FC** measured **income distance** from the **average of the top three large States'** per capita GSDP — option **(2)**.
Others are wrong: demographic performance = **population growth 1971-2011** (not TFR); forest **includes open forests**; **GDP contribution replaced tax effort**, not the reverse.
xa: 16th FC weights: income distance **42.5**, population 2011 **17.5**, area **10**, forest **10**, demographic performance **10**, GDP **10**.
Forest also counts the **increase in forest area (2015-2023)**.
GDP criterion = **square root of State GSDP** over the sum of square roots.

60.s: Andhra Pradesh's 'prosperity paradox' in tax devolution arises under which criterion?
60.x: Income distance gives greater weight to States with lower per capita GSDP, so Andhra Pradesh's above-average per capita income works against it.
xa: The 16th FC measures income distance from the **average of the top three large States**.
The new **GDP-contribution** criterion helped AP's share rise.
AP's 16th FC share: **4.217%**; tax share in **AP Budget 2026-27**: **4.22%**.

60.s: The Fifteenth Finance Commission assigned the highest weight among the following to which criterion?

60.tq: Compare the principal weight with the three moderately weighted criteria.
xs: **Income distance** got the highest weight under the 15th FC, at **45** — option **(1)**.
Others: **population 2011 – 15**, **demographic performance – 12.5**, **forest and ecology – 10**.
xa: Income distance was the highest weight in **every FC** (16th: **42.5**).
15th FC also used **area 15** and **tax and fiscal effort 2.5**.
15th FC chair: **N.K. Singh**; vertical share **41%**.

60.s: What is Andhra Pradesh's share in tax devolution under the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
60.x: AP's share rose to 4.217% from 4.05%; all five southern States gained.

60.s: How is demographic performance measured by the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
60.x: The 16th FC measures demographic performance by population growth 1971-2011; the 15th FC used change in TFR.

60.s: What weight did the Fifteenth Finance Commission give to demographic performance in horizontal devolution?
60.x: The 15th FC gave demographic performance a weight of 12.5%.

60.s: What weight did the Fourteenth Finance Commission give to forest cover in horizontal devolution?
60.x: The 14th FC gave forest cover 7.5%; the 15th and 16th FCs gave forest and ecology 10%.

60.s: What weight did the Sixteenth Finance Commission give to income distance in horizontal devolution?
60.x: Income distance got 42.5% under the 16th FC (45% in the 15th, 50% in the 14th); it is still the highest weight.

60.s: What is the transfer of work to field officers within the bureaucracy, without transfer to elected local bodies, called?

xs: **N. Chandrababu Naidu v UoI (2019)** raised the random VVPAT–EVM tally from **one to five polling stations** per **Assembly segment** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The tally unit is the **Assembly segment**, not a district or parliamentary constituency.
xa: **ADR v ECI (Apr 2024)** rejected **100% slip counting** and a **return to paper ballots**.
In that case, symbol-loading units are sealed for **45 days**; runners-up can seek a check of **5% of EVMs**.
**Subramanian Swamy v ECI (2013)**: VVPAT is needed for free and fair polls; introduce it **in phases**.

64.s: VVPAT slips must be counted in which of the following circumstances?
o: Whenever EVM data and Form 17C do not match
Whenever postal ballots exceed the number of EVM votes
Only in constituencies using postal ballots
Only when the winning candidate requests it after the declaration of results
64.x: VVPAT slips are required to be counted wherever the EVM data and Form 17C do not match.
64.tq: Apply the verification rule to a specific discrepancy rather than to a general recount demand.
xs: **VVPAT slips must be counted wherever EVM data do not match Form 17C** — so option **(1)** is correct.
This is one of the **new ECI rules** on counting; postal ballots relate to a different rule (below).
xa: The **penultimate EVM/VVPAT round** is counted only after **postal ballots** are finished.
**ADR v ECI (April 2024)**: candidates placed **2nd and 3rd** can seek a check of **5% of EVMs' burnt memory** within **7 days**.
ECI objects that **totalisers** would make **EVM, VVPAT and Form 17C** checks harder.

64.s: Which State was the first to conduct its entire Assembly election using EVMs?
64.x: Goa conducted the first whole-State Assembly election using EVMs in 1999. Gujarat was not the first State to do so.
64.tq: Separate pilot use from the first whole-State use.
xs: **Goa, 1999** was the first whole-State Assembly election on EVMs — option **(2)**.
⚠ **Gujarat** was **not** the first; **Kerala** (**Parur 1982**) was the first pilot; **Nagaland** (Noksen) = first **VVPAT**.
xa: APPSC-G2 **2025** key: the Goa 1999 statement is true.
**2004** = first nationwide (all-India) EVM use.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
64.x: VVPAT was introduced on 4 September 2013; EVMs were first used on 19 May 1982, EPIC rolled out in 1993 and NOTA on 27 September 2013.
n: Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were first used experimentally on 19 May 1982. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) was first used on 4 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
None of the Above (NOTA) was implemented on 27 September 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
VVPAT was introduced before NOTA in 2013. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
NOTA was mandated later in September 2013 than VVPAT was introduced. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: ⚠ **VVPAT** came **before NOTA** in **2013**.
**Section 61A** (RPA 1951) gave EVMs statutory backing in **1989**.
**2004** = first all-EVM Lok Sabha election.

64.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Goa (1999) – First State-wide Assembly election using EVMs
Parur Assembly Constituency – First experimental use of EVM
14th Lok Sabha election (2004) – First nationwide general election entirely using EVMs
64.x: VVPAT was first introduced in Noksen Assembly Constituency; Goa saw the first all-EVM State poll.
n: The first experimental use of EVMs occurred in the Parur Assembly Constituency in Kerala. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The first VVPAT use occurred in the Noksen Assembly Constituency in Nagaland. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
Goa was the first State to conduct an entire General Assembly election using EVMs across all constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The 14th Lok Sabha General Election in 2004 was the first nationwide general election conducted entirely using EVMs. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: ⚠ **Gujarat** was **not** the first State to use EVMs in an Assembly election.
Noksen VVPAT use was a **by-election** on **4 September 2013**.
EVM makers: **BEL** (Bengaluru) and **ECIL** (Hyderabad).

64.s: An M3 EVM control unit can connect up to how many ballot units?
64.x: An M3 system can take up to 24 ballot units (384 candidates including NOTA), whereas M2 supports four ballot units and 64 candidates.
xa: EVMs are to show **colour photos** of candidates.
First pilot: **70-Parur, Kerala, 1982**.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about VVPAT?
o: The slip is handed over to the voter for personal custody
It prints a slip with the serial number, name and symbol of the selected candidate
The voter can see the printed slip for seven seconds
It is attached to the Electronic Voting Machine
64.x: The voter only views the slip through the VVPAT window; it is not handed over.
xa: Generations: **M1, M2, M3** (current).
First used at **51-Noksen, Nagaland, 2013**.

64.s: What is the principal purpose of a Remote Voting Machine (RVM) prototype?
o: To permit domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station
To count postal ballots together with EVM votes
To enable overseas citizens to vote in all constituencies without registration
To conceal booth-wise voting patterns by pooling control units
64.x: The ECI's RVM prototype is intended to enable domestic migrants to vote for up to 72 constituencies from one remote polling station.
64.tq: Distinguish remote voting from totaliser-based secrecy of booth results.
xs: The **RVM** lets **domestic migrants** vote for up to **72 constituencies** from one remote polling station — option **(1)**.
Pooling control units to hide booth-wise trends is the **totaliser**, not the RVM.
xa: RVM was demonstrated to parties in **Jan 2023**.
**Overseas electors** were enabled by the RP (Amendment) Act **2010**.

64.s: At how many electors per polling station did the Election Commission fix the cap?
64.x: The ECI capped the number of electors per polling station at 1,200, down from the earlier 1,500.

64.s:
Which of the following is the correct order of counting-related procedures?
A. Counting of postal ballots
B. Counting of the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round
C. Counting of the final EVM/VVPAT round
64.x: Postal ballots are counted before the penultimate EVM/VVPAT round; the final EVM/VVPAT round follows subsequently.
64.tq: Arrange the procedure by identifying the expressly stated precedence of postal-ballot counting.
xs: Order: **postal ballots** → **penultimate EVM/VVPAT round** → final round — option **(1)**.
The penultimate round is counted only after postal ballots are finished.
xa: VVPAT slips are counted wherever EVM data do not match **Form 17C**.
Runners-up can seek a **5%** EVM check within **7 days**.

64.s:
Consider the following statements about EVMs:
1. They were first used at Parur, Kerala, in 1982.
2. Gujarat was the first State to hold its entire Assembly election on EVMs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Only statement 1 is correct: Goa (1999), not Gujarat, was the first whole-State Assembly poll on EVMs.

64.s: An M3 EVM control unit can handle up to how many candidates, including NOTA?
64.x: One M3 control unit takes 24 ballot units, i.e. 384 candidates including NOTA; the M2 took 64.

64.s: For how long is a VVPAT slip visible to the voter through the window?
64.x: The VVPAT slip is shown for 7 seconds and is not handed to the voter.

64.s: The 2004 election to the 14th Lok Sabha was the first of which of the following?
o: National election held entirely on EVMs
64.x: 2004 was the first all-EVM national election; VVPAT and NOTA came in 2013.

64.s: A Remote EVM (RVM) can handle up to how many constituencies from one remote polling station?
64.x: The RVM, for domestic migrants, can cover up to 72 constituencies from one remote station.

64.s: How many candidates can an M2 EVM with four ballot units handle?
64.x: An M2 EVM takes 4 ballot units, that is 64 candidates; an M3 control unit takes 24 ballot units, or 384 candidates including NOTA.

64.s: Which case arose from the first use of EVMs at Parur (Kerala) in 1982?
o: N. Chandrababu Naidu v Union of India
64.x: The 1982 Parur EVM trial was challenged in A.C. Jose v Sivan Pillai; Section 61A then gave EVMs statutory backing in 1989.

64.s: Which two public sector undertakings manufacture EVMs in India?
64.x: EVMs are made by Bharat Electronics Ltd (Bengaluru) and Electronics Corporation of India Ltd (Hyderabad).

64.s: In which year was NOTA first used in a Lok Sabha election?
64.x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections; its first Lok Sabha use was in 2014.

64.s: In which year was the Electors' Photo Identity Card (EPIC) introduced?
64.x: EPIC was introduced in 1993 and its number stays valid for life despite a change of address; it did not come through the 61st Amendment.
xa: PYQ order: **EVM → photo ID → VVPAT → NOTA** (**UPPSC 2025**).
**Election Laws (Amendment) Act 2021**: **Aadhaar linking** of rolls to stop multiple enrolment.
EVMs were first used in **1982** (**Parur, Kerala**) — before EPIC.

64.s: Which law provided for linking electoral rolls with Aadhaar to check multiple enrolment?
o: Representation of the People Act, 1950 as originally enacted
64.x: The Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021 provided Aadhaar linking, multiple qualifying dates, gender-neutral wording and requisition of premises.
xa: **2022**: spending limit raised to **₹95 lakh (LS) / ₹40 lakh (Assembly)** for bigger States.
**2025**: **ECINET**, one platform for **40+ apps**; **100% webcasting**; **Special Intensive Revision (SIR)** of rolls.
**Overseas electors**: RP (Amendment) Act **2010**, in force **Feb 2011**.

64.s: Who make up the selection panel under the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners Act, 2023?
o: The Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Union Home Minister
The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of India and the Leader of the Opposition
64.x: The 2023 Act provides for a panel comprising the Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister, and the Leader of the Opposition. The Chief Justice of India was dropped from the panel.
64.tq: Use the composition trap by identifying the authority omitted from the final arrangement.
xs: The **2023 Act** panel = the **Prime Minister**, a **Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM** and the **Leader of the Opposition** — so option **(2)** is correct.
The **CJI was dropped**; a panel of **PM, LoP and CJI** was the **Tarkunde Committee**'s **1975** proposal.
xa: ⚠ **Tarkunde (1975)** panel had the **CJI**; the **2023 Act** dropped the CJI.
Criticism: the Act gives the **executive a majority** on the panel that picks the election referee.
The **Law Commission 255th Report (2015)** proposed a **collegium** for appointing the CEC.

64.s: Under which Chief Election Commissioner was the nationwide rollout of Electors Photo Identity Cards started in 1993?
64.x: The nationwide EPIC rollout began in 1993 under Chief Election Commissioner T.N. Seshan.
n: Electors Photo Identity Cards (EPICs) had their nationwide rollout initiated in 1993. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
The nationwide rollout of EPICs was initiated under Chief Election Commissioner T. N. Seshan. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xa: EPIC was introduced to prevent **bogus voting** and **impersonation**.
An EPIC number, once issued, is **valid for life**.
PYQ order: **EVM → photo ID → VVPAT → NOTA** (UPPSC 2025).

64.s: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly elections of which of the following States?
64.x: NOTA was first used in the 2013 Assembly polls of Chhattisgarh, Mizoram, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Delhi.

64.s: Under the CEC and Other ECs Act, 2023, who was dropped from the selection panel?
64.x: The 2023 Act panel is the PM, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM and the LoP; the CJI was dropped.

Arrange the following electoral reforms in chronological order:

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
64.x: Section 61A came in 1989, EPIC in 1993, the two-seat cap in 1996 and Aadhaar linking by the Election Laws (Amendment) Act, 2021.

64.x: The ECI-SEC declaration of 26 February 2026 was made under CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

64.s: What was the Supreme Court of India ruling on the Electoral Bond Scheme?
o: The scheme was uphold as constitutional
The scheme was struck down as unconstitutional
The scheme was modified to include more transparency measures
The scheme was deferred for further reviews
64.src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
64.x: In ADR v Union of India (15 Feb 2024) a five-judge bench unanimously struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme as unconstitutional, as it violated voters' right to information under Art. 19(1)(a).

64.s:
Consider the following Statements about 'Electoral Bonds'

A. A citizen of India or a body incorporated in India will be eligible to purchase the Electoral Bonds

B. Electoral Bonds would be purchased for any value of Rs 1000 maximum up to 1 crore from specified branches of State Bank of India.

C. Electoral Bonds would have a life of only 15 days during which it can be used for making donations only to political parties registered under section 29A of Representation of People Act 1951.

D. Electoral bonds are donated to a political party which secured not less than 1% of votes polled in the last general assembly elections.
Which of the above statement is/are correct?
64.x: All four are correct: bonds could be bought by a citizen or a body incorporated in India, in values from Rs 1,000 to Rs 1 crore at SBI, were valid for 15 days, and could go only to a 29A-registered party with at least 1% of the votes in the last election.

64.s:
Consider following statements about Electoral Bond Scheme 2018:
(A) The aim of this scheme is to bring about transparency in the funding process of political parties.
(B) Only the political parties recognized by the Election Commission which secured not less than two percent of the votes polled in the last general election to the House of People or the Legislative Assembly of the State shall be eligible to receive the Electoral Bonds.
(C) Electoral Bonds shall be valid for fifteen calendar days from the date of issue.
(D) The Electoral Bond deposited by an eligible political party in its account shall be credited on the same day.
Which of the above statements are correct?
64.x: Aim (transparency), the 15-day validity and same-day credit are correct. The eligibility threshold was not less than 1% of the votes in the last Lok Sabha or Assembly election, not 2%.

64.s:
Consider following statements about Electoral Bond Scheme 2018.

I. The aim of this scheme is to bring about transparency in the funding process of political parties.

II. Only the political parties recognised by the Election Commission which secured not less than two per cent of the votes polled in the last general election to the House of People or the Legislative Assembly of the State shall be eligible to receive the Electoral Bonds.

III. Electoral Bonds shall be valid for fifteen calendar days from the date of issue.

IV. The Electoral Bond deposited by an eligible political party in its account shall be credited on the same day.
Which of the above statements are correct?
64.x: Aim (transparency), the 15-day validity and same-day credit are correct. The eligibility threshold was not less than 1% of the votes in the last Lok Sabha or Assembly election, not 2%.

64.s: For a political party to retain tax exemption under the stated provisions, which combination is relevant?
o: No donation above ₹2,000 in any form and no record of larger donations
No cash donation above ₹20,000 and records only of donations above ₹2,000
No cash donation above ₹2,000 and proper records of donations above ₹20,000
Acceptance of unlimited cash donations provided they are reported after the election
64.x: The stated conditions include no cash donation above ₹2,000 and maintenance of records for donations above ₹20,000. These are referred to under Section 12 of the Income Tax Act, 2025, replacing the earlier reference to Section 13A of the 1961 Act.
64.tq: Keep the two monetary thresholds separate instead of reversing their functions.
xs: **No cash donation above Rs 2,000** and **records of donations above Rs 20,000** — option **(3)**.
Option (2) swaps the two thresholds.
xa: ⚠ **Rs 2,000** = cash cap; **Rs 20,000** = record threshold.
Now under **Sec. 12, Income Tax Act 2025**; earlier **Sec. 13A**, IT Act **1961**.

64.s: According to ADR, about what share of political parties' funds in 2004-23 came from undisclosed sources?
64.x: ADR found that 60% (₹19,083 crore) of party funds in 2004-23 came from undisclosed sources.

64.s: Under which Section of the Income-tax Act, 2025 do political parties get tax exemption?
64.x: Party tax exemption is now in Section 12 of the Income-tax Act, 2025; earlier it was Section 13A of the 1961 Act.

64.s: In ADR v Union of India (2024), on what main ground did the Supreme Court strike down the Electoral Bond Scheme?
o: The right to equality under Article 14
The voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a)
The right to life under Article 21
The freedom of association under Article 19(1)(c)
64.x: The five-judge bench unanimously held that donor anonymity violated voters' right to information, part of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a). Articles 14, 21 and 19(1)(c) were not the ground stated for striking the scheme down.
64.tq: Bonds struck down = Art 19(1)(a) right to information (15 Feb 2024).
xs: The scheme violated voters' **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)** — option **(2)**.
Articles **14**, **21** and **19(1)(c)** were not the stated ground.
xa: **PUCL (2003)**: voter's **right to know** is part of Art. 19(1)(a).
**PUCL (2013)**: right to reject (NOTA) also flows from Art. 19(1)(a).

64.s: The Supreme Court's decision in Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India also invalidated which change associated with electoral political funding?
o: Abolition of political party registration under the RPA
Removal of the corporate donation cap under the Companies Act
Compulsory disclosure of all cash donations by parties
Restriction on donations by individual citizens
64.x: The Court struck down the removal of the corporate donation cap from the Companies Act.
64.tq: Identify the allied legal provision affected by the judgment, not merely the main scheme.
xs: It also struck down the **removal of the corporate donation cap** from the **Companies Act** — option **(2)**.
The notes record no ruling on party registration, cash disclosure or individual donations.
xa: Ground: violation of voters' **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)**.
ADR: **60% (₹19,083 cr)** of party funds in **2004-23** came from undisclosed sources.

64.s: A political party could encash electoral bonds only if it had secured at least what percentage of votes in the last election?
64.x: Only a registered political party that had secured at least 1% of the votes in the last election could encash electoral bonds.
64.tq: Recall the statutory eligibility threshold rather than the general registration requirement.
xs: A party could encash electoral bonds only with at least **1 per cent** (**1% of the vote**) in the last election — so option **(2)** is correct.
Only **registered parties** meeting this **1%** threshold could encash; the bonds were sold only by **SBI** as **bearer bonds**.
xa: Denominations: **₹1,000 to ₹1 crore**; each bond was valid for **15 days**.
The scheme was notified in **2018** via **Finance Act 2017** amendments.
Struck down as **unconstitutional** by a unanimous **five-judge Constitution Bench** in **ADR v UoI** (**15 Feb 2024**) — it violated the **right to information under Art. 19(1)(a)**.
⚠ Donor anonymity was hailed in older notes as a "**transparency**" gain.

64.s: In the 2024 electoral bond judgment, whom did the Supreme Court direct to give donor data to the Election Commission?
64.x: A five-judge Constitution Bench unanimously struck down the scheme and directed SBI to provide donor data to the ECI.
xa: Case: **ADR v Union of India, 15 Feb 2024**.
⚠ **ADR v UoI** 2002 = disclosure; **ADR v ECI** 2024 = EVM/VVPAT.

64.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about electoral bonds?
o: They were sold only by the State Bank of India
They were issued in denominations from ₹1,000 to ₹10 crore
64.x: The denominations ran from ₹1,000 to ₹1 crore, not ₹10 crore; SBI was the only seller and the bearer bonds were valid for 15 days.

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: 2013 — Lily Thomas judgment striking down Section 8(4) of the RPA
2002 — Disclosure of criminal record, assets and education
64.x: Electoral bonds were struck down by the Supreme Court in 2024; they were not introduced in that year. The other pairs are correctly matched.
64.tq: Find the reversed action-year pair, particularly where a later year records invalidation rather than introduction.
xs: **2024 — Introduction of electoral bonds** is wrongly matched — so option **(4)** is the answer.
Electoral bonds were notified in **2018** and **struck down** in **2024** (**ADR v UoI**, **15 Feb 2024**).
The rest are correct: **Lily Thomas** struck down **Sec. 8(4)** in **2013**; **ADR v UoI** (**2002**) mandated disclosure; **EVMs** in all constituencies in **2004**.
xa: ⚠ **ADR v UoI** **2002** = disclosure; **2024** = electoral bonds; **ADR v ECI** **2024** = EVM/VVPAT.
Bonds were sold only by **SBI**, in **₹1,000 to ₹1 crore** denominations, valid **15 days**.
The verdict was by a unanimous **five-judge Constitution Bench**, under the **right to information** (**Art. 19(1)(a)**).

64.s: Who could buy electoral bonds?
o: Only companies listed on a stock exchange
A citizen of India or a body incorporated in India
64.x: Bonds could be bought by a citizen of India or a body incorporated in India, alone or jointly.

64.s: On which date was the Electoral Bond Scheme notified?
64.x: The scheme was notified on 2 January 2018 and struck down on 15 February 2024.

64.s: By which bench was the 2024 electoral bonds verdict in ADR v Union of India delivered?
64.x: A five-judge bench unanimously held the scheme unconstitutional.

64.s: Through which law was the Electoral Bond Scheme brought in?
64.x: The Electoral Bond Scheme was notified on 2 January 2018 on the basis of the Finance Act, 2017.

64.s: A candidate contesting the elections forfeits deposit, if he does not secure
o: 1/6th of the total votes polled and valid
1/2nd of the total votes polled and valid
1/3rd of the votes polled and valid
64.x: A candidate forfeits the security deposit if he fails to secure more than one-sixth (1/6) of the total valid votes polled in the constituency.

64.s: Which section of the Representation of People's Act was interpreted by Supreme Court recently, while ruling that votes cannot be sought in the name of religion, race, caste, community or language?
64.src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
64.x: In Abhiram Singh v C.D. Commachen (2 Jan 2017) a 7-judge bench interpreted Section 123(3) of the RPA, 1951 (corrupt practices): votes cannot be sought in the name of religion, race, caste, community or language.

64.s: If in an election to a State Legislative Assembly the candidate who is declared elected loses his deposit, it means that –
o: The election was for a multi-member constituency
The elected candidate’s victory over his nearest rival
A very large number of candidates contested
64.x: A candidate loses his deposit if he fails to get more than one-sixth of the valid votes. If even the winner gets less, the votes were split among a very large number of candidates. Poor polling or a narrow margin would not by itself cause this.

64.s:
Consider the following statements:

1. In India, there is no law restricting the candidates from contesting in one Lok Sabha election from three constituencies.

2. In 1991 Lok Sabha Election, Shri Devi Lal contested from three Lok Sabha constituencies.

3. As per the existing rules, if a candidate contests in one Lok Sabha election from many constituencies, his/her party should bear the cost of bye-elections to the constituencies vacated by him/her in the event of him/her winning in all the constituencies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
64.x: Only 2 is correct: Devi Lal contested three Lok Sabha seats in 1991. Statement 1 is wrong – Sec. 33(7) of the RPA (1996) limits a candidate to two constituencies; 3 is wrong – no rule makes the party pay for the bye-elections.

64.s: The highest number of Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections were held in India during the decade of:
64.x: The 1990s saw the most Lok Sabha and Assembly elections (Lok Sabha in 1991, 1996, 1998 and 1999) because of frequent changes of government and hung Houses.

64.s: Which Section of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 bans exit polls?
64.x: Section 126A of the RPA, 1951 concerns the ban on exit polls.
xa: Liquor ban **48 hours** before poll = **Sec. 135C**.
Paid holiday on poll day = **Sec. 135B**.

64.s: A candidate forfeits the security deposit when the candidate fails to secure more than which proportion of the total valid votes polled?
64.x: A candidate loses the security deposit if they win no more than one-sixth of the valid votes.
n: A candidate forfeits the security deposit if the candidate fails to secure more than one-sixth of the total valid votes polled. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
xs: The deposit is forfeited if the candidate fails to get more than **one-sixth** of the **total valid votes** — option **(4)**.
**Sec. 34** deposits: **₹25,000** (Lok Sabha), **₹10,000** (Assembly), half for SC/ST.
xa: The **1996** RP (Amendment) Act brought **higher security deposits**.
It also required more proposers for independents/unrecognised parties.
Election petition: within **45 days** (**Sec. 81**).

64.s: Under Section 33(7) of the RPA, 1951, from how many constituencies at most can a candidate contest a Lok Sabha or Assembly election?
64.x: Section 33(7), added in 1996, limits a candidate to two constituencies.
n: Section 33 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, limits a candidate to contesting from a maximum of two constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
A candidate can contest from a maximum of two Lok Sabha constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]
A candidate can contest from a maximum of two State Assembly constituencies. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #25 · pp 62-65]

64.s: Disclosure of criminal antecedents of candidates is dealt with in which Section of the RPA, 1951?
64.x: Section 33A concerns disclosure of criminal antecedents; Section 8 is disqualification, 29A registration and 123 corrupt practices.

64.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the corrupt practices covered by Section 123 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951?
o: Failure to file an election expenditure account within 30 days
Appeal on the grounds of religion or caste
64.x: Section 123 covers corrupt practices such as bribery, undue influence and appeals based on religion or caste. Filing the expenditure account within 30 days is governed by Section 78.
64.tq: Find the provision belonging to a neighbouring compliance area rather than the corrupt-practices list.
xs: **Failure to file an expense account within 30 days** is not a Sec. 123 corrupt practice — option **(1)**; it falls under **Sec. 78**.
**Sec. 123** covers **bribery, undue influence, appeal on religion/caste**.
xa: Failure to file accounts can lead the **ECI** to **disqualify** the candidate.
Bribery and undue influence are now offences in **BNS** too.

64.s: Within how many days must a person elected from two constituencies vacate one of them?
64.x: Under Section 70 one seat must be vacated within 14 days; the two-constituency cap in Section 33(7) came with the 1996 amendment.
xa: **30 days** is the deadline for filing expense accounts (**Sec. 78**).

64.s: Which Section of the RPA, 1951 requires a candidate to keep an account of election expenses?
64.x: Section 77 requires the account to be kept; Section 78 requires it to be filed with the DEO within 30 days.

64.s: Under Section 34 of the RPA 1951, what is the security deposit for a general-category Lok Sabha candidate?
64.x: It is ₹25,000 for the Lok Sabha and ₹10,000 for an Assembly; SC/ST candidates pay half.

64.s: What does Section 81 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 relate to?
o: Corrupt practices during an election campaign
The maintenance of election expenditure accounts
Election petitions presented in the High Court within 45 days of the result

xs: **Sec. 81** = **election petition** in the **High Court** within **45 days** — option **(4)**.

64.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Section 70 — Disqualification under the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971

xs: **Sec. 151A — by-election within six months** is correct — option **(3)**.

64.s: Section 61A was inserted into the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in which year to provide statutory backing to Electronic Voting Machines?

Section 61A was added to the Representation of the People Act, 1951, in 1989. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #73 · pp 199-201]
xs: **Section 61A** was added to the RPA 1951 in **1989** — option **(3)** — giving EVMs **statutory** backing.

64.s: Which of the following statements is incorrect regarding the death of a contesting candidate?
o: The election is automatically cancelled in every case of the death of a candidate.
The death of a candidate no longer automatically countermands the election.
The change was made through the 1996 Amendment.
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement within a set timeframe.
64.x: Option A is incorrect: since the 1996 amendment, a candidate's death no longer cancels the election automatically. A recognised party can name a replacement within a set time.
64.tq: Recall the 1996 change on a candidate's death.
n: The Representation of the People Act, 1951 was amended in 1996 to cap the number of constituencies a candidate could contest at two. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Before the 1996 amendment, elections were automatically countermanded upon the death of a contesting candidate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
After the 1996 amendment, elections are no longer automatically countermanded upon the death of a contesting candidate. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
Recognized political parties may nominate a replacement for a deceased contesting candidate within a set timeframe. [Indian Polity · ROCKET SHEET #53 · pp 141-144]
xs: The incorrect statement is that the election is **automatically cancelled** on every candidate's death — option **(1)**.
After the **1996 amendment**, death **no longer** automatically countermands the election.
A **recognised political party** may **nominate a replacement** within a set timeframe.
xa: **Countermanding** now happens only on the death of a **recognised-party** candidate.
The **1996** Act also made poll day a **paid holiday** (**Sec. 135B**) and banned liquor **48 hours** before poll (**Sec. 135C**).
Bypolls within **6 months** (**Sec. 151A**).

Capping a candidate’s contest to two constituencies and increasing security deposits

xs: The **RP (Amendment) Act, 1996** capped contests at **two constituencies** and raised **security deposits** — option **(4)**.

xa: It limited **countermanding** to the death of a **recognised-party** candidate.
It added a **paid holiday** (**Sec. 135B**) and **liquor ban** (**Sec. 135C**).
Offences under the **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971** became a disqualification.

64.s: With reference to India, which of the following statements about Indian political parties is correct?
